`toast({endContent})` takes text, a Node or a Lit template.
Renamed `uniqueId`; a `toast()` option (de-duplication belongs to the viewport).

hooks.notes: `toast(options, {from})` returns the dismiss function; `dismissToast(uniqueId)` and `dismissAllToasts()` complete it. The first call registers the elements.
Swipes never start on interactive descendants (the shared selector list).
Internal element (@internal): top-layer popover host, stacking, F6, focus hand-off, announcements.

keyboard.action: Moves focus into the newest toast (its trailing action first, then the close button)
keyboard.when: a toast is showing and focus is outside the notifications region

keyboard.action: Activates the focused close button or trailing action; dismissing a focused toast hands focus to a remaining toast, or back to where it was
Moves between the toast's controls; leaving the toast resumes the auto-hide countdown

differences.text: `isAutoHide` and `autoHideDuration` are one property: `auto-hide-duration` in ms, `0` keeps the toast (`autoHide: false` in `toast()`), unset means 5000 for `info` and `0` for `error`. `uniqueID` is `uniqueId`; `useToast()` is `toast()` (plus `dismissToast()` and `dismissAllToasts()`); `onDismiss` and `onHide` are the events `tct-toast-dismiss` and `tct-toast-hide` (also `onHide` in the `toast()` options); toast positions are kebab case (`bottom-end`).

The toast has status/alert semantics but `aria-live="off"`: the viewport speaks each toast once through the announcer (A§10). Upstream stamps a live region on the card and announces separately, which reads a toast twice on some assistive technology.
`tct-toast` never removes itself: it fires `tct-toast-dismiss` (cancelable), sets `exiting` and fires `tct-toast-hide` once; the owner (the viewport, or your listener) removes it after the exit.

No drop shadow (D-013): the inverted fill separates the card from the page. The ink is `light-dark(--color-on-dark, --color-on-light)` (`--color-on-error` for errors) because the media-theme island attribute cannot reach into a shadow tree; the close button uses the double focus ring for inverted surfaces (D-005).
The swipe transform is applied through `translate`/`scale` (individual transform properties); the exit slide only runs without reduced motion, the fade stays.

requests.reason: An inverted-surface hook for a ghost icon-only button (for example `--button-fg` / `--button-bg-hover` or a `data-surface=inverted` variant) would let the toast dismiss button become a tct-button; today the private `--_fg`/`--_bg` tokens cannot be reached from outside the shadow root.

Two new core event classes, `tct-toast-dismiss` and `tct-toast-hide`, were added in packages/core/src/events/ (flags and payload are asserted in toast/tct-toast.test.ts); add them to the shared events test if the orchestrator wants them listed there.

core.toast.notes: Guides: [mwg:persistent-toast-notifications] [mwg:persistent-top-layer-ui] [mwg:animate-to-from-top-layer]. The close button stays a native <button> around tct-icon: it sits on the inverted card and tct-button has no colour hooks for inverted surfaces (see requests). The viewport host is itself the popover, so the shared .layer-surface class does not apply.

api.notes: The whole `{position, maxVisible, inset}` object; the attributes `toast-position` and `toast-max-visible` and the property `toastInset` (structured data is property-only) win over its fields.

hooks.notes: `toast()` reaches the outermost connected provider; `toast(options, {from})` the nearest one around an element.
A nested provider does nothing, like upstream.

differences.text: The `toast` config is also available as `toast-position` and `toast-max-visible` attributes (declarative use) and a `toastInset` property; `position` values are kebab case (`bottom-end`).

Upstream hosts the sheet and imperative-modal layers in the same provider; here only the toast viewport is hosted. Bottom sheets and alert dialogs are elements, and `openAlertDialog()` renders its own dialog, so they need no provider.

core.layer-provider.notes: Provider: no shadow root and no box (A§8.1); the light-dom rule ships in tct-layer-provider.light.css and is adopted at runtime.
